facts.raw_span: A young black woman with sickle cell disease (HbSS variant)
2-day history of visual loss in the left eye
No dehydration or other precipitating factors were noted
Visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/800 OS
peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions
ischemic macular whitening was noted
No cherry-red spot, hemorrhage, or peripheral neovascularization was present
abnormal retinal capillary bed across the macula, with increased intercapillary spacing and small areas of hypofluorescence nasal to the fovea
Hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL, corresponding to ophthalmoscopically opaque areas
Temporal macular thinning
retinal atrophy
atrophy of middle retinal layers

concepts.why: Patient has sickle cell disease and presents with peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions and hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL.
Patient presents with sudden visual loss in one eye and ischemic macular whitening, consistent with a retinal vascular occlusion.
Patient has abnormal retinal capillary bed and temporal macular thinning, indicating retinal ischemia.
Patient has sickle cell disease and presents with retinal atrophy and atrophy of middle retinal layers, consistent with sickle cell maculopathy.
Patient presents with visual loss and ischemic macular whitening, consistent with a retinal vascular occlusion.
Patient has a genetic component to their disease, with retinal atrophy and hyperreflective plaques, consistent with a hereditary retinal dystrophy.
Patient presents with ischemic macular whitening and abnormal retinal capillary bed, consistent with ischemic maculopathy.
Patient has retinal atrophy and atrophy of middle retinal layers, consistent with retinal degeneration.

rationales.F01: Sickle cell disease is a known risk factor for sickle cell retinopathy and maculopathy.
rationales.F04: Visual acuity loss is a common symptom of retinal diseases.
rationales.F05: Peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions are characteristic of sickle cell retinopathy.
rationales.F06: Ischemic macular whitening is a sign of retinal ischemia.
rationales.F08: Abnormal retinal capillary bed is a characteristic of sickle cell retinopathy and retinal ischemia.
rationales.F09: Hyperreflective plaques are a characteristic of sickle cell retinopathy.
rationales.F12: Atrophy of middle retinal layers is a sign of retinal degeneration and ischemia.
